rationale: Both role-isolated advisory inputs were present from distinct runs and model families, pinned to the same frozen candidate. The academic review returned request-changes with five major findings and one minor; the learning-design review approved. No finding carries blocking severity, and every one was correctable in this single finalization pass, so the findings were disposed here rather than returned. The decisive one was a sourcing error: the interval for judging whether a presentation is independent of drinking had been attributed to the wrong figure in its source. Checked directly against the article, which carries a two-to-four-week period for deciding about medication and at least three months for reviewing a psychiatric history; the lesson now states both with the question each answers. A second finding criticised a repair made in the previous revision, which had replaced a broken taxonomy with one that discarded prior likelihood; the position now holds both truths. The academic verdict stands as dissent and no reviewer has seen the repaired text.
dissent: The academic review's request-changes verdict stands as material dissent from the candidate as reviewed. Its findings were incorporated by the maintainer afterwards; no reviewer has approved the repaired text.

The maintainer records a further reservation of its own, against itself: this outcome was authored out of learner order at a prerequisite depth of roughly eighteen topics, almost none of which exists as a lesson. It has drawn substantive majors in two independent rounds. The repairs are real; the structural position is unchanged, and the outcome should be re-authored once its prerequisites exist.
